mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about an egg that a hen laid on Yom Tov: may we eat it that day? They also argue about how much chametz on Pesach is forbidden.

chunks.en: An egg that a hen laid on Yom Tov:
chunks.st: With regard to an egg that was laid on a Festival
chunks.stMore: (Eduyyot 4:1),

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say: it may be eaten.
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: It may be eaten
chunks.stMore: even on that day,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say: it may not be eaten.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say: It may not be eaten,
chunks.stMore: as the Gemara will explain at length. Apropos this exceptional case, in which Beit Shammai are lenient and Beit Hillel are strict, the mishna cites additional halakhot of the Festivals in which this unusual phenomenon occurs (Yoma 79b).

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: For sourdough, the forbidden amount is the size of an olive,
chunks.st: Leaven, i.e., dough that has leavened to such an extent that it is no longer used as food but as a leavening agent for other dough, is prohibited on Passover in the measure of an olive-bulk.

words.note: Very sour dough, used to make other dough rise.

chunks.en: and for chametz bread, it is the size of a big date.
chunks.st: However, the measure for edible leavened bread is greater, that of a large date-bulk.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: for both, it is the size of an olive.
chunks.st: For both this and that, the measure is that of an olive-bulk.

mishnayos.summary: After shechting a wild animal or a bird, we must cover its blood with earth. This mishnah asks how to do that on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: If someone shechts a wild animal or a bird on Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: Then there is a mitzvah to cover its blood with earth.
chunks.st: Furthermore, with regard to one who slaughters an undomesticated animal or a bird on a Festival
chunks.stMore: (Eduyyot 4:2), in which case there is a mitzva from the Torah to cover the blood after slaughtering (Leviticus 17:13),

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he may dig up earth with a shovel and cover the blood.
chunks.st: He digs earth with a shovel and covers the blood with that earth ab initio.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: He should not shecht at all,
chunks.st: He may not slaughter ab initio,

chunks.en: unless he had
chunks.st: unless he had

chunks.en: earth ready from before Yom Tov.
chunks.st: earth prepared for that purpose while it was still day.

chunks.en: But they agree that if he already shechted,
chunks.st: But even Beit Hillel concede that if one already slaughtered
chunks.stMore: the animal or the bird,

chunks.en: he should dig with a shovel and cover the blood.
chunks.st: then he should dig with a shovel and cover the blood.

chunks.en: And ashes from a stove count as ready to use.
chunks.st: Additionally, they agree that the ashes of a stove are considered prepared for the use of covering blood, as will be explained by the Gemara.

mishnayos.summary: More arguments about Yom Tov: may we carry a ladder to the dovecote to take young doves, and how must we pick out the doves before Yom Tov?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.he: אֵין מוֹלִיכִין אֶת הַסֻּלָּם מִשּׁוֹבָךְ לְשׁוֹבָךְ,
chunks.en: We may not carry a ladder from one dovecote to another,
chunks.st: One may not carry a ladder, which was used for reaching doves, from one dovecote to another.

words.note: A dovecote is a little house where doves live.

chunks.en: but he may tilt it from one window to another.
chunks.st: However, one may move it slightly so that he tilts it from one window to another in the same dovecote.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel permit even carrying a ladder from one dovecote to another.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say: he may not take young doves
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say: One may not take
chunks.stMore: fledgling doves from a dovecote on a Festival,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִעֲנֵעַ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
chunks.en: unless he shook them before Yom Tov.
chunks.st: unless he shook the ones he wished to take while it was still day, thereby preparing them.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.he: עוֹמֵד וְאוֹמֵר זֶה וָזֶה אֲנִי נוֹטֵל:
chunks.en: he stands before Yom Tov and says: I will take this one and that one.
chunks.st: It is not necessary to shake; rather, it is sufficient if one stands the day before and says: I will take this fledgling and that one.

mishnayos.summary: Someone picked out young doves before Yom Tov to use on Yom Tov. What if he finds different doves the next day?

chunks.en: If he picked out black doves and found white ones,
chunks.st: If, on the eve of a Festival, one designated black fledglings to be slaughtered, and on the following day found white
chunks.stMore: ones in the dovecote, rather than the birds he had designated,

chunks.en: or white ones and found black ones,
chunks.st: or if one designated white ones to be slaughtered and found black
chunks.stMore: ones,

chunks.en: or two and found three, they are forbidden.
chunks.explain: These may not be the doves he picked.
chunks.st: or if one designated two fledglings to be slaughtered and found three, they are prohibited,
chunks.stMore: as these are not the same fledglings he had designated earlier.

chunks.en: If he picked three and found two, they are allowed.
chunks.explain: We say one of them flew away.
chunks.st: If, however, one designated three to be slaughtered and found only two, they are permitted,
chunks.stMore: as it is presumed that one of the fledglings escaped.

chunks.en: If he picked them inside the nest and found them in front of the nest,
chunks.st: If one designated them inside the nest and the next day he cannot find them there, and he found fledglings before the nest,

chunks.he: אֲסוּרִים. וְאִם אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא הֵם,
chunks.en: they are forbidden. But if those are the only doves there,
chunks.st: they are prohibited, as they might be fledglings other than the ones he designated and left inside the nest. But if there are only those fledglings in the immediate vicinity,

chunks.en: they are allowed.
chunks.st: they are permitted, as it can be assumed that these are the ones he designated inside the nest.

mishnayos.summary: More arguments between Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel about what we may move or carry on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.he: אֵין מְסַלְּקִין אֶת הַתְּרִיסִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: We may not take down the shutters of a store on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: One may not remove the shutters [terisin] of a store on a Festival,
chunks.stMore: due to the prohibition against building and demolishing.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow even putting them back.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel permit one not only to open the shutters, but even to replace them.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may not take the big pestle
chunks.st: One may not take a large pestle
chunks.stMore: from a mortar, which is normally used for crushing wheat in the preparation of porridge, for any other purpose on a Festival, e.g.,

words.note: A heavy wooden club for crushing wheat.

chunks.en: to cut meat on it.
chunks.st: to cut meat on it;

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel permit it.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Likewise, Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may not put a raw animal skin
chunks.st: One may not place an unprocessed hide

chunks.en: where people will step on it,
chunks.explain: Stepping on it helps make leather, which is work.
chunks.st: before those who will tread on it,
chunks.stMore: as this constitutes the prohibited labor of tanning on a Festival.

chunks.he: וְלֹא יַגְבִּיהֶנּוּ, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ
chunks.en: and he may not lift it, unless there is
chunks.st: And one may not lift the hide from its place, as it is considered muktze, unless there is

chunks.en: an olive's size of meat on it.
chunks.st: an olive-bulk of meat on it,
chunks.stMore: in which case it may be carried on account of its meat;

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel permit it in both cases.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may not carry out a small child,
chunks.st: One may carry out on a Festival neither a minor child,

chunks.en: or a lulav, or
chunks.st: nor a lulav,

chunks.en: a Sefer Torah into the street.
chunks.st: nor a Torah Scroll into the public domain,
chunks.stMore: as none of these are required for the preparation of food;

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel permit it.

mishnayos.summary: May we bring challah and other gifts to a Kohen on Yom Tov? Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue and give their reasons.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may not bring challah or the other gifts
chunks.st: One may not bring separated ḥalla or any of the other priestly gifts, i.e., the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw of a slaughtered animal,

words.note: Parts of an animal that are given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: to a Kohen on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: to a priest on a Festival,
chunks.stMore: though it is permitted to separate them from an animal slaughtered on a Festival.

chunks.en: whether they were taken off the day before,
chunks.st: This is prohibited regardless of whether they were separated last evening, i.e., before the Festival,

chunks.en: or they were taken off today.
chunks.st: or whether they were separated today.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel permit it.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:

chunks.en: We can compare them:
chunks.st: This halakha can be derived by an analogy:

chunks.en: Challah and the gifts are a gift to the Kohen,
chunks.st: Ḥalla and the other gifts are both considered a gift to the priest,

chunks.en: and terumah is a gift to the Kohen.
chunks.st: and likewise teruma separated from produce is also a gift to the priest.

chunks.en: Just as we may not bring terumah on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: Just as you agree that one may not bring teruma to a priest on a Festival,

chunks.en: so we may not bring the gifts.
chunks.st: so too, one may not bring the other gifts.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to them:
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to them:

chunks.en: No! You said this about terumah,
chunks.st: No, this analogy is incorrect. If you said that you derive the halakha from teruma,

chunks.en: which we may not take off on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: where its separation is not allowed on the Festival,

chunks.en: Can you say it about the gifts,
chunks.st: how will you say the same with regard to the gifts from an animal or ḥalla,

chunks.en: which we may take off on Yom Tov?
chunks.st: concerning which their separation is allowed on the Festival?
chunks.stMore: Since it is not prohibited to separate these gifts, they may likewise be brought to a priest.

mishnayos.stIntro: The separation of ḥalla is permitted on a Festival, as one is permitted to prepare dough and bake it on a Festival, and bread may not be eaten without first separating ḥalla.

mishnayos.summary: How may we crush spices and salt on Yom Tov? Beis Shammai say we must do it in a different way than on a weekday.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: Spices may be crushed with a wooden pestle,
chunks.st: Spices may be pounded on a Festival in a slightly unusual manner, with a wooden pestle,

chunks.en: and salt with a clay jug
chunks.st: and salt may be pounded only with an earthenware flask

chunks.en: or with a wooden spoon.
chunks.st: or with a wooden pot ladle,
chunks.stMore: in a manner very different from that of a weekday.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.he: תְּבָלִין נִדּוֹכִין כְּדַרְכָּן בְּמָדוֹךְ שֶׁל אֶבֶן,
chunks.en: Spices may be crushed in the usual way, even with a stone pestle,
chunks.st: Spices may be pounded in their usual manner, even with a stone pestle,

chunks.en: and salt with a wooden pestle.
chunks.st: and as for salt, although it must be pounded in an irregular manner, a slight modification such as pounding it with a wooden pestle
chunks.stMore: is enough to render the act permitted.

mishnayos.summary: How may we pick the bad pieces out of beans on Yom Tov?

chunks.en: Someone who sorts beans on Yom Tov:
chunks.st: With regard to one who selects legumes on a Festival
chunks.stMore: by separating the edible and inedible portions,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he picks out the food and eats it right away.
chunks.st: He may select food and eat it immediately,
chunks.stMore: while leaving the refuse.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he may sort in his usual way, in his lap,
chunks.st: He may select in his usual manner, in his lap,

chunks.en: in a basket or in a bowl,
chunks.st: with a tray, or with a large vessel,

chunks.en: but not on a board,
chunks.st: but he may not do so with a tablet,

chunks.en: or with a sifter, or with a sieve.
chunks.explain: These are special sorting tools, so it looks like weekday work.
chunks.st: nor with a winnow, nor with a sieve,
chunks.stMore: as these vessels are specially designed for selecting, which gives his action the appearance of a weekday activity.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel says:

chunks.en: he may even wash them and take off the bad bits that float up.
chunks.st: One may even wash the legumes in water and skim off the refuse floating on top.

mishnayos.summary: What gifts may we send to a friend on Yom Tov?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.he: אֵין מְשַׁלְּחִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב אֶלָּא מָנוֹת.
chunks.en: On Yom Tov we may send only portions of cooked food.
chunks.st: One may send only portions of prepared food on a Festival, but not any other gifts.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: we may send animals and birds,
chunks.st: One may even send gifts of domesticated animals, undomesticated animals, and fowl,

chunks.en: whether alive or shechted.
chunks.st: whether alive or slaughtered.

chunks.en: We may send wine, oil, flour and beans,
chunks.st: Similarly, one may send wines, oils, and vessels of flour, and even legumes,

chunks.en: but not grain,
chunks.explain: Grain must be ground first, and we may not grind on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: but not grain,
chunks.stMore: which is unfit for use, as one may not grind it on the Festival.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Shimon allows grain.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Shimon permits sending gifts even in the case of grain, as it can be made into porridge without being ground.

mishnayos.summary: We may send clothes and things as presents on Yom Tov, as long as they can be used on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: We may send clothes,
chunks.st: One may send clothes,

chunks.en: whether they are sewn or not sewn,
chunks.st: whether they are sewn or whether they are unsewn,

chunks.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן כִּלְאַיִם,
chunks.en: even if they have shaatnez in them,
chunks.st: and even if they contain diverse kinds,
chunks.stMore: a prohibited mixture of wool and linen [sha’atnez].

chunks.en: as long as they are for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: But one may do so only if they serve the purposes of the Festival.

chunks.en: But not a sandal with nails in it,
chunks.explain: The Rabbis said not to wear it on Shabbos and Yom Tov.
chunks.st: However, one may not send a spiked sandal,
chunks.stMore: which has nails fixed to it, as the Sages decreed that one may not wear a sandal of this kind on a Shabbat or Festival,

chunks.en: or a shoe that is not sewn.
chunks.st: nor an unsewn shoe,
chunks.stMore: which is not suitable for a Festival.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Not even a white shoe,
chunks.st: One may not even send a white shoe,
chunks.stMore: which people do not usually wear,

chunks.en: because it needs a craftsman to color it.
chunks.st: because it requires an artisan to paint it black.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the general principle:

chunks.en: Anything that we may use
chunks.st: Anything that one may use

chunks.en: on Yom Tov, we may send it.
chunks.st: on a Festival, one may send it.

mishnayos.summary: When Yom Tov is on Friday, we may not cook on Yom Tov for Shabbos, unless we made an eruv tavshilin before Yom Tov.

chunks.he: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: When Yom Tov falls on Friday,
chunks.st: With regard to a Festival that occurs on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: a person may not cook from the start
chunks.st: one may not cook on the Festival with the initial intent to cook

chunks.en: on Yom Tov for Shabbos.
chunks.st: for Shabbat.

chunks.en: But he may cook for Yom Tov,
chunks.st: However, he may cook on that day for the Festival itself,

chunks.en: and if some is left over,
chunks.st: and if he left over any food,

chunks.en: it is left over for Shabbos.
chunks.st: he left it over for Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: The early Sages also instituted an ordinance: The joining of cooked foods [eiruv tavshilin], which the mishna explains.

chunks.en: He may make a cooked dish before Yom Tov
chunks.explain: This is called an eruv tavshilin.
chunks.st: One may prepare a cooked dish designated for Shabbat on a Festival eve

chunks.en: and count on it to cook on Yom Tov for Shabbos.
chunks.st: and rely on it to cook on the Festival for Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: The tanna’im disagreed with regard to the details of this ordinance:

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: You need two cooked dishes.
chunks.st: For the purpose of the joining of cooked foods one must prepare two cooked dishes,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: One dish is enough.
chunks.st: One dish is sufficient.

chunks.en: They agree that a fish with an egg on it
chunks.st: And they both agree with regard to a fish and the egg that is fried on it

chunks.en: counts as two dishes.
chunks.st: that these are considered two dishes for this purpose.

chunks.en: If he ate it, or it got lost,
chunks.st: If one ate the food prepared before the Festival as an eiruv and none of it remained for Shabbat, or if it was lost,

chunks.en: he may not count on it to start cooking for Shabbos.
chunks.st: he may not rely on it and cook with the initial intent to cook for Shabbat.

chunks.en: But if he left even a little bit of it,
chunks.st: If he left any part of the eiruv,

chunks.en: he may count on it for Shabbos.
chunks.st: he may rely on it to cook for Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: When Yom Tov is on Sunday, when may people and keilim be dipped in a mikveh to become tahor for Yom Tov?

chunks.en: If Yom Tov falls right after Shabbos,
chunks.st: If a Festival occurs directly after Shabbat, i.e., on a Sunday,
chunks.stMore: and one wishes to behave in a proper manner and purify himself and his vessels in honor of the Festival,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: everything must be dipped in a mikveh before Shabbos.
chunks.st: One must immerse everything before Shabbat,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: Keilim must be dipped before Shabbos,
chunks.st: Vessels must be immersed before Shabbat,

chunks.en: but a person may dip himself on Shabbos.
chunks.st: but a person may immerse himself even on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: How can tamei water be made tahor on Yom Tov? And which kinds of dipping in a mikveh are allowed on Yom Tov?

chunks.en: They agree that we may let tamei water touch the mikveh water
chunks.st: And Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel both agree that one may bring ritually impure water into contact with ritually pure water

chunks.en: in a stone vessel, to make it tahor.
chunks.explain: A stone vessel cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: in stone vessels on Shabbat in order to purify the water.
chunks.stMore: Impure water can be purified if it is placed into a vessel that does not contract ritual impurity, such as a stone vessel, and then lowered with the vessel into a ritual bath. The water becomes purified when it comes into contact with the water of the ritual bath. Although this is not considered proper immersion, water may nevertheless be purified in this manner.

chunks.en: But we may not dip it in a tamei vessel.
chunks.explain: That would make the vessel tahor too, which is not allowed.
chunks.st: However, one may not immerse the impure water in a ritually impure vessel in order to purify the vessel at the same time.

chunks.en: And we may dip keilim to use them for a holier purpose, or with a different group.
chunks.explain: The keilim are already tahor; this makes them ready for something more special.
chunks.st: Likewise, one may immerse on a Festival from one principle to another, and from one group to another, as will be explained in the Gemara.
chunks.basisNote: The meaning of the last phrase follows Bartenura.

mishnayos.summary: Which korbanos may be brought on Yom Tov, and may we lean our hands on them?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may bring shelamim, but we may not lean our hands on them.
chunks.st: One may bring peace-offerings on a Festival, but one may not place his hands on them,
chunks.stMore: as this is considered using animals, which is prohibited on a Festival by rabbinic decree.

chunks.en: But we may not bring olos.
chunks.explain: On Yom Tov we may shecht only to make food for people.
chunks.st: However, one may not bring burnt-offerings,
chunks.stMore: apart from the obligatory daily and additional offerings of the day, because burnt-offerings are consumed entirely on the altar and not by people, and slaughter is permitted on a Festival only for the purpose of human consumption.

words.note: Burnt-offerings, which are burned completely on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: we may bring shelamim and olos, and lean our hands on them.
chunks.st: One may bring both peace-offerings and burnt-offerings, and one may even place his hands on them.

mishnayos.summary: May we heat water on Yom Tov to wash our feet? And may we make a fire to keep warm?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: A person may not heat water for his feet,
chunks.st: A person may not heat water on a Festival in order to wash his feet

chunks.en: unless it is also good for drinking.
chunks.st: unless it is also fit for drinking,
chunks.stMore: as they hold that kindling a fire on a Festival is permitted only for the sake of preparing food, but not for washing.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: But Beit Hillel permit one to kindle a fire on a Festival even for washing.

chunks.en: A person may make a fire and warm himself by it.
chunks.st: A person may kindle a large fire and warm himself at it.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel was strict like Beis Shammai in three things. The Sages said his family was strict for themselves but not for everyone.

chunks.en: In three things Rabban Gamliel
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel was stringent about three things

chunks.en: is strict like Beis Shammai:
chunks.st: in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: We may not wrap up hot food to keep it warm
chunks.st: One may not insulate hot food

chunks.en: on Yom Tov for Shabbos;
chunks.st: on a Festival for Shabbat ab initio, but rather one ought to do so on the eve of the Festival;

chunks.he: וְאֵין זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: we may not stand up a menorah that fell on Yom Tov;
chunks.st: and one may not set up a metal candelabrum that fell on a Festival;

chunks.he: וְאֵין אוֹפִין פִּתִּין גְּרִיצִין אֶלָּא רְקִיקִין.
chunks.en: and we may not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
chunks.st: and one may not bake thick loaves on a Festival but only thin ones,
chunks.stMore: due to the great effort entailed in preparing the former.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: In my father's house, they never
chunks.st: From the days of my father’s household

chunks.en: baked thick loaves on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: they would never bake thick loaves on a Festival,

chunks.en: only thin ones.
chunks.st: but only thin ones.

chunks.en: The Sages said to him:
chunks.st: The Sages said to him:

chunks.en: What can we do about your father's house?
chunks.st: What shall we do for your father’s household,

chunks.en: They were strict with themselves
chunks.st: who were stringent with themselves

chunks.en: but lenient for all of Klal Yisrael,
chunks.st: but lenient with all of the Jewish people,

chunks.en: letting them bake thick loaves and cakes baked on coals.
chunks.st: to allow them to bake thick loaves and cakes baked on coals.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Gamliel was lenient in three things, but the Sages forbid them.

chunks.he: אַף הוּא אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דְבָרִים לְהָקֵל,
chunks.en: He also said three things to be lenient:
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel also said three things as leniencies,
chunks.stMore: in opposition to the view of most of the Sages:

chunks.en: We may sweep the dining room on Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: They used to lean on couches while eating.
chunks.st: One may sweep the room of the couches on a Festival, i.e., the dining room,
chunks.stMore: where they would recline on couches to eat, as there is no concern that by sweeping the room one might come to fill in the holes and level the ground.

chunks.en: we may put sweet-smelling spices on coals on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And one may place incense consisting of fragrant herbs on burning coals in order to perfume one’s house on a Festival.

chunks.en: and we may make a whole roasted young goat on the night of Pesach.
chunks.st: And one may prepare a whole kid goat, meaning a kid goat roasted whole, with its entrails over its head, on the night of Passover,
chunks.stMore: as was the custom when they roasted the Paschal lamb in the Temple.

chunks.en: But the Sages forbid all three.
chunks.st: However, the Rabbis prohibit all three practices: It is prohibited to sweep lest one come to level the ground, it is prohibited to burn incense because it does not meet the criteria of permitted food preparation, and it is prohibited to eat a kid that was roasted whole on the night of Passover because it would appear as if he were eating consecrated food outside the Temple.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah allowed three things that the Sages forbid, about caring for animals and grinding pepper.

chunks.en: There are three things Rabbi Elazar
chunks.st: There are three things

chunks.en: ben Azaryah allows
chunks.st: that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya permits

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid:
chunks.st: and the Rabbis prohibit:

chunks.en: His cow went out on Shabbos with a strap between its horns.
chunks.explain: The Sages say the strap is a load, not jewelry.
chunks.st: His cow would go out on Shabbat with a decorative strap between its horns.
chunks.stMore: Rabbi Elazar holds that such a strap is considered an ornament for the cow rather than a burden, whereas the Sages view it as a burden.

chunks.en: We may comb an animal with a fine comb on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And one may comb [mekardin] an animal with a fine comb on a Festival
chunks.stMore: in order to remove ticks and dirt from its hair; the Rabbis prohibit this due to a concern that he might thereby come to wound or bruise the animal.

chunks.en: and we may grind pepper in its own mill.
chunks.st: And one may grind pepper needed on the Festival even in its own mill,
chunks.stMore: although this appears similar to a weekday labor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אֵין מְקָרְדִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בְיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not comb an animal with a fine comb on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One may not comb an animal to remove ticks and dirt from its hair on a Festival

chunks.en: because it makes a sore.
chunks.st: because this certainly creates a wound,

chunks.en: But we may brush it with a soft comb.
chunks.st: but one may brush it with a wooden comb, as its blunt teeth do not wound the animal.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: We may not comb, and not even brush.
chunks.st: One may not comb, nor may one even brush.

mishnayos.summary: A pepper mill is made of three parts, and each part can become tamei on its own.

chunks.en: A pepper mill can become tamei
chunks.st: The aforementioned pepper mill
chunks.stMore: is a composite vessel, and each of its parts must be considered independently with respect to ritual impurity.

chunks.en: because it is three keilim:
chunks.st: It is susceptible to ritual impurity because of each of the three vessels of which it is comprised:

chunks.en: because it is a vessel that holds things,
chunks.st: It is susceptible to impurity because it is a wooden receptacle,

chunks.en: because it is a metal vessel,
chunks.st: it is susceptible to impurity because it is a metal vessel,

chunks.en: and because it is a sifter.
chunks.st: and it is susceptible to impurity because it is a sieve.

mishnayos.summary: A child's wagon can become tamei. May we pull it along the ground on Shabbos?

chunks.en: A child's toy wagon can become tamei from being sat on,
chunks.st: A child’s wagon, with which he plays and upon which he also sits, is susceptible to ritual impurity imparted by treading.
chunks.stMore: It is considered a fixed seat of the child, so that if the child is a zav and he sits on the wagon, it contracts the ritual impurity imparted by the treading of a zav.

words.note: Midras: a kind of tumah that comes from sitting or leaning on a thing.

chunks.en: and it may be moved on Shabbos.
chunks.st: And this wagon may be handled on Shabbat, as it is considered a vessel.

chunks.he: וְאֵינָהּ נִגְרֶרֶת אֶלָּא עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים.
chunks.en: But it may be pulled only over cloths.
chunks.explain: Otherwise it would make a groove in the ground, like plowing.
chunks.st: And it may be dragged on the ground on Shabbat only upon cloth,
chunks.stMore: a stone pavement, or the like, as otherwise it would create a furrow when dragged, and one would be liable due to the prohibited labor of plowing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: No keilim may be pulled on the ground
chunks.st: For this reason, no vessels may be dragged on the ground on Shabbat

chunks.en: except a wagon,
chunks.st: except for a wagon,

chunks.en: because it only presses the earth down.
chunks.st: which is permitted because its wheels do not make a furrow in the ground but merely press the earth down. Since no earth is moved from its place, this is not considered digging or plowing on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Tov we may not trap fish or animals, because trapping is not allowed. But an animal that is already easy to grab may be taken.

chunks.he: אֵין צָדִין דָּגִים מִן הַבֵּיבָרִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not catch fish from their ponds on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One may not trap fish from their ponds on a Festival
chunks.stMore: even with the intention of eating them, as this falls into the category of hunting, a type of labor that is not permitted on a Festival.

chunks.en: and we may not put food in front of them.
chunks.explain: Fish find their own food in the water.
chunks.st: Nor may one place food before them,
chunks.stMore: as it is not his duty to feed them; rather, they maintain themselves by eating smaller fish or different types of algae that grow in the water.

chunks.he: אֲבָל צָדִין חַיָּה וָעוֹף מִן הַבֵּיבָרִין,
chunks.en: But we may catch an animal or a bird from their pens,
chunks.st: However, one may trap an animal or a bird from their enclosures [beivarim],
chunks.stMore: as they are viewed as already captured, and therefore the action is not considered an act of hunting.

chunks.en: and we may put food in front of them.
chunks.st: And one may also place food before them as one does for other household animals.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Not all pens are the same.
chunks.st: Not all enclosures are identical with respect to the halakhot of hunting.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Any animal that still needs to be chased and caught is forbidden,
chunks.st: With regard to any animal inside such an enclosure whose trapping is inadequate,
chunks.stMore: meaning that the enclosure is large and contains hiding places so that it is still necessary to pursue and apprehend the animal, it is prohibited for one to catch it;

chunks.en: and any animal that does not need to be chased is allowed.
chunks.st: and with regard to any animal whose trapping is not inadequate,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible to seize it immediately without having to engage in further pursuit, it is permitted for one to catch it.

mishnayos.summary: Traps set before Yom Tov: may we take what is in them on Yom Tov? And a story about Rabban Gamliel and some fish.

chunks.en: Traps for animals, birds and fish
chunks.st: If traps for animals, birds, and fish

chunks.en: that were set before Yom Tov:
chunks.st: were set on the eve of a Festival,

chunks.en: he may not take anything from them on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: one may not take anything from them on the Festival,

chunks.en: unless he knows
chunks.st: unless he knows that

chunks.en: that they were caught before Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the animals found in the traps had already been caught on the eve of the Festival.

chunks.en: Once, a non-Jew
chunks.st: And an incident is related where a certain gentile

chunks.en: brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,
chunks.st: brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,

chunks.en: and he said: They are allowed,
chunks.st: and the latter said: The fish are permitted,

chunks.en: but I do not want to take them from him.
chunks.st: but I do not wish to accept them from him, as I despise him.

mishnayos.summary: When may we shecht an animal on Yom Tov if it is about to die? And how do we carry the meat home?

chunks.en: An animal that is about to die, he may not shecht it on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: If an animal is in danger of dying, in which case its meat would be prohibited as the animal had not been properly slaughtered, and one wishes to slaughter it in the hope that it will be found fit for eating and he will be spared a loss, he may not slaughter it on a Festival

chunks.en: unless there is still time
chunks.st: unless there is still time in the day

chunks.en: in the day to eat an olive's size of it roasted.
chunks.explain: Then we can say he shechted it for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: for him to eat an olive-bulk of roasted meat from the animal,
chunks.stMore: so that it is possible to say that he slaughtered the animal for the sake of the Festival.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: Even enough time to eat an olive's size raw, from where it was shechted.
chunks.st: There need not be enough time for him to roast it; rather, it is sufficient even if there is only time to eat an olive-bulk of raw meat from the place where the animal is slaughtered,
chunks.stMore: i.e., from its neck, without going to the trouble of removing its hide and roasting it.

chunks.en: If he shechted it in the field,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered an animal on a Festival in the field,

chunks.en: he may not bring it home on a pole or on two poles,
chunks.st: he may not bring it to his house on a pole or on a set of poles
chunks.stMore: carried by two people, as this appears similar to a weekday activity.

chunks.en: but he brings it in his hand, piece by piece.
chunks.st: Rather, he must alter his usual weekday manner of performing this action and bring it in by hand, limb by limb. A male firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats belonging to a Jew is sanctified from birth and must be given to a priest to be sacrificed on the altar in the Temple. If a firstborn animal acquired a physical blemish that disqualifies it from being sacrificed as an offering, it still must be given to a priest, but it may be redeemed, slaughtered, and eaten as non-sacred meat.

mishnayos.summary: A bechor animal fell into a pit on Yom Tov. May we take it out and shecht it?

chunks.en: A bechor animal that fell into a pit:
chunks.st: If a firstborn animal fell into a cistern on a Festival, and there is concern that it might die there,

words.note: A firstborn animal. It may be eaten only if it has a mum.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: An expert should go down and look at it.
chunks.st: An expert in these matters goes down into the cistern and examines the animal.

chunks.en: If it has a mum,
chunks.st: If it has a permanent blemish,
chunks.stMore: owing to which it may be slaughtered and eaten,

words.note: A blemish, a mark that makes it unfit for a korban.

chunks.en: he may bring it up and shecht it.
chunks.st: he may raise it from the cistern and slaughter it;

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: but if it does not have a blemish, or if its blemish is temporary,

chunks.en: he may not shecht it.
chunks.st: he may not slaughter it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִכָּר מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
chunks.en: Any bechor whose mum was not known before Yom Tov
chunks.st: Even if it has a blemish, it is prohibited to slaughter it, as any firstborn animal whose blemish is not perceptible while it is still day, i.e., on the day before the Festival,

chunks.en: is not ready to be used on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: is not considered to be among the animals prepared prior to the Festival for use on the Festival.

mishnayos.summary: An animal that died on Yom Tov, and challah that became tamei, may not be moved.

chunks.en: An animal that died
chunks.st: With regard to an animal that died,

chunks.en: may not be moved from its place on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: one may not move it from its place on a Festival.

chunks.en: Once they asked Rabbi Tarfon
chunks.st: And such an incident once occurred and they asked Rabbi Tarfon

chunks.en: about this, and about challah that became tamei.
chunks.explain: Tamei challah may not be eaten or used on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: about it. And on that same occasion they also asked him about ḥalla that had been separated from dough and then became ritually impure on a Festival.
chunks.stMore: Such ḥalla is not fit to be eaten by anyone, nor may it be used in any other manner, e.g., as animal feed or as fuel for a fire, on that day.

chunks.en: He went into the beis midrash and asked,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon entered the study hall and inquired
chunks.stMore: about these matters,

chunks.en: and they told him:
chunks.st: and the Sages said to him:

chunks.en: They may not be moved from their place.
chunks.st: One may not move them from their place.

mishnayos.summary: People may share one animal on Yom Tov if they agreed before Yom Tov. We may not use a scale on Yom Tov.

chunks.he: אֵין נִמְנִין עַל הַבְּהֵמָה לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not sign up to share an animal for the first time on Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: Making a deal like this looks like buying and selling.
chunks.st: One may not register to have a portion of an animal on a Festival ab initio,
chunks.stMore: since it is prohibited to divide up an animal into portions for different people, as this is similar to conducting business, a weekday activity, on a Festival.

chunks.he: אֲבָל נִמְנִין עָלֶיהָ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
chunks.en: But we may sign up for it before Yom Tov,
chunks.st: But one may register for the animal on the eve of the Festival,

chunks.en: and then shecht it and divide it between them.
chunks.st: and then those who registered for the animal may slaughter and divide it between them
chunks.stMore: on the Festival itself in accordance with the agreement reached the day before. The next day, each pays the slaughterer according to his portion of the animal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.stMore: A person selling meat on a Festival who wishes to know its weight in order to determine its price may not weigh it against regular weights in the ordinary weekday manner, but he may

chunks.en: A person may weigh meat against a vessel
chunks.st: weigh the meat against a vessel

chunks.en: or against a cleaver.
chunks.st: or against a cleaver [kofitz]
chunks.stMore: and then calculate the weight of the meat by weighing the vessel or cleaver later.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כָּל עִקָּר:
chunks.en: We may not use a scale at all.
chunks.st: One may not look at the pans of a balance scale at all, meaning that they may not be used for weighing in any manner or for any other purpose.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Tov we may not sharpen a knife the usual way, and we may not buy meat by price.

chunks.he: אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not sharpen a knife on Yom Tov the usual way.
chunks.st: One may not sharpen a knife on a Festival in the ordinary weekday manner.

chunks.en: But he may rub it against another knife.
chunks.st: However, one may do so in an unusual fashion, e.g., to run one knife over another,
chunks.stMore: thereby sharpening the blade.

chunks.en: A person should not say to a butcher on Yom Tov:
chunks.st: A person may not say to a butcher on a Festival:

chunks.en: Weigh me a dinar's worth of meat.
chunks.explain: Talking about money makes it look like weekday business.
chunks.st: Weigh for me a dinar’s worth of meat,
chunks.stMore: since if he mentions a sum of money, it looks like a commercial transaction.

chunks.en: But he may shecht and they divide it among themselves.
chunks.st: But the butcher may slaughter an animal and apportion it among his customers without stipulating a price.

mishnayos.summary: We may not measure things the usual way on Yom Tov. The mishnah tells how Abba Shaul ben Botnis filled his measures before Yom Tov, and how we may ask a storekeeper for eggs and nuts by number.

chunks.en: A person may say to his friend on Yom Tov:
chunks.st: One person may say to another on a Festival:

chunks.en: Fill this vessel for me,
chunks.st: Fill this vessel for me,
chunks.stMore: and I will return its contents or reimburse you after the Festival,

chunks.en: but not with a measuring cup.
chunks.st: but he may not ask him to fill the vessel in a particular measure.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it was a measuring cup,
chunks.st: If it was a measuring utensil,

chunks.en: he may not fill it.
chunks.st: he may not fill it.

chunks.en: There was a story with Abba Shaul ben Botnis,
chunks.st: There was an incident involving Abba Shaul ben Botnit, a Sage who was also a grocer,

chunks.he: שֶׁהָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדּוֹתָיו מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
chunks.en: who would fill his measures before Yom Tov
chunks.st: who would fill his measures on the eve of a Festival

chunks.en: and give them to his customers on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: and give them to his customers on the Festival.
chunks.stMore: In this way he would know exactly how much he had given each person, without conducting any measurements on the Festival itself.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul, a Sage distinct from Abba Shaul ben Botnit, says:

chunks.en: He did this even on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: He would do this even on the intermediate days of a Festival

chunks.en: so the measures would be exact.
chunks.st: because of the clarity of the measures,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in order to clarify precisely how much must be given to each customer, since the measurement is more precise once the foam of the liquid being measured has subsided.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: He did this even on a weekday,
chunks.st: Even on a weekday it is proper to do so,

chunks.en: so every drop could drip out of the measures.
chunks.st: because of the draining of the measures.
chunks.stMore: This method allows all the liquid to drain fully out of the seller’s measuring utensil so that the amount is exact.

chunks.he: הוֹלֵךְ אָדָם אֵצֶל חֶנְוָנִי הָרָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ,
chunks.en: A person may go to a storekeeper he usually buys from
chunks.st: A person may go on a Festival to a grocer from whom he is accustomed to buy

chunks.en: and say to him:
chunks.st: and say to him:

chunks.en: Give me this many eggs and nuts,
chunks.st: Give me eggs and nuts of such-and-such a number,

chunks.en: because a person usually
chunks.st: as it is the manner of a homeowner

chunks.en: counts them in his own house.
chunks.st: to count this way in his own house. Counting eggs or nuts is not considered a commercial activity, as people regularly mention the number of eggs and nuts that they need.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Tov we should carry things in a different way than on a weekday. And which straw and wood may we take for the fire?

chunks.en: Someone who brings jugs of wine from one place to another
chunks.st: One who brings wine jugs from one place to another place

chunks.en: may not bring them in a basket or a box,
chunks.explain: That is the weekday way of carrying many jugs.
chunks.st: may not bring a large number of them in a basket or in a tub
chunks.stMore: in the usual weekday manner on a Festival, as this is disrespectful of the Festival;

chunks.he: אֲבָל מֵבִיא הוּא עַל כְּתֵפוֹ אוֹ לְפָנָיו.
chunks.en: but he may carry them on his shoulder or in front of him.
chunks.st: but he may bring one or two barrels on his shoulder or carry them in front of himself.

chunks.en: And so, someone who carries straw
chunks.st: Similarly, one who brings straw
chunks.stMore: for kindling or for feeding animals

chunks.en: may not swing the box onto his back,
chunks.st: may not place the tub behind him
chunks.stMore: while carrying it, as this is the usual weekday manner;

chunks.en: but he may carry it in his hand.
chunks.st: but he may transport it in front of him in his hand,
chunks.stMore: in an unusual fashion.

chunks.en: We may start taking straw from a pile,
chunks.st: And one may begin taking straw for kindling from the pile of straw,
chunks.stMore: although he did not designate the pile for this purpose the day before;

chunks.en: but not from the wood in the storage yard.
chunks.st: but one may not begin to take from the wood in the wood storage, a small yard behind the house where people store various items that they do not intend to use in the near future.

words.en: that is in the storage yard

mishnayos.summary: Which wood may we take for the fire on Yom Tov? Not from a sukkah, and only from wood that was ready from before Yom Tov.

chunks.en: We may not take wood from a sukkah,
chunks.explain: Taking it would be like breaking down a building.
chunks.st: One may not take wood from a sukka
chunks.stMore: on any Festival, not only on the festival of Sukkot, because this is considered dismantling,

chunks.en: only from what is next to it.
chunks.st: but one may take from near it.

chunks.he: מְבִיאִין עֵצִים מִן הַשָּׂדֶה מִן הַמְכֻנָּס,
chunks.en: We may bring wood from a field only from a pile,
chunks.st: One may bring wood chopped from a tree the previous day from an unfenced field, but only from that which has been gathered
chunks.stMore: into a pile before the Festival for the purpose of using it for kindling. However, scattered wood is muktze and may not be handled.

chunks.en: and from a karpef, even wood that is scattered.
chunks.st: And if one brings wood from a karpef used for storage, he may bring even from the scattered wood,
chunks.stMore: as it is considered a guarded courtyard rather than a field, and one does not remove even scattered items from his mind if they are stored inside such an enclosure.

words.note: A fenced yard used for keeping things.

chunks.en: What is a karpef?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: What is a karpef?

chunks.en: Any one near the city.
chunks.st: It is any enclosure that is near a city, but if it is far from a city, it is considered a field;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Any one that we go into with a key,
chunks.st: Any fenced place into which one can enter only with a key is a karpef, even if it is located at a distance from a city,

chunks.en: as long as it is within the techum Shabbos.
chunks.st: provided that it is within the Shabbat limit.

words.note: The limit of how far we may walk out of town on Shabbos.

mishnayos.summary: How may we chop wood on Yom Tov? And may we take fruit out of a closed storeroom that has a hole?

chunks.en: We may not chop wood
chunks.st: One may not chop wood

chunks.en: from building beams,
chunks.st: on a Festival neither from beams intended for construction

chunks.he: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְיוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: or from a beam that broke on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: nor from a beam that broke on a Festival,
chunks.stMore: although it no longer serves any purpose.

chunks.en: And we may not chop with an ax,
chunks.st: And one may not chop wood on a Festival, neither with an ax,

chunks.en: or with a saw, or with a sickle,
chunks.st: nor with a saw, nor with a sickle,
chunks.stMore: as these are clearly craftsman’s tools used on weekdays.

chunks.en: only with a cleaver.
chunks.st: Rather, one may chop only with a cleaver.
chunks.stMore: Using this tool differs greatly from the weekday manner in which wood is chopped.

chunks.en: A storeroom full of fruit
chunks.st: If there is a house that is filled with produce

chunks.en: that was closed up and a hole opened in it:
chunks.st: and locked on all sides, and a hole formed in one of its walls or its roof,

chunks.en: he may take fruit out through the hole.
chunks.st: one may remove produce through the place of the hole.
chunks.stMore: The produce is not considered muktze, even though one cannot reach it without the existence of the hole.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: He may even make a hole from the start and take fruit.
chunks.st: One may even make a hole ab initio and take produce through that opening.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Tov we may not make a new lamp, make charcoal, or cut a wick with a knife.

chunks.en: We may not shape a clay lamp on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: On a Festival, one may not hollow out a piece of clay to form a lamp
chunks.stMore: into which he will place oil and a wick

chunks.en: because he is making a new vessel.
chunks.st: because he thereby creates a vessel.

chunks.en: We may not make charcoal on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not produce charcoal at all on a Festival
chunks.stMore: because this is not labor for sustenance.

chunks.en: and we may not cut a wick in two.
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not cut the wick,
chunks.stMore: as this is considered mending a vessel.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He may cut it with fire, for two lamps.
chunks.explain: He lights it in the middle, between two lamps.
chunks.st: If one requires a wick of a particular length, he may cut it by burning it in a fire but not by cutting it with a knife.
chunks.basisNote: How it is done follows Bartenura.

mishnayos.summary: More things we may not do on Yom Tov, because they are like weekday work or like building.

chunks.en: We may not break a piece of clay on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One may not break earthenware on a Festival.

chunks.en: and we may not cut paper
chunks.st: And one may not cut paper

chunks.en: to roast salted fish on it.
chunks.st: in order to roast salted fish on it.
chunks.stMore: Earthenware shards or pieces of paper that have been soaked in water were placed on the metal surface or in the oven in which the fish was roasted, so that it would not be burned by the heat.

chunks.en: We may not sweep out an oven or a stove,
chunks.st: And one may not sweep out anything that has fallen into an oven or stove that interferes with the baking, such as plaster.

chunks.en: but we may press down the ashes.
chunks.st: But one may press down
chunks.stMore: and flatten any accumulated dust and ashes at the bottom of the oven, which might prevent it from lighting properly.

chunks.en: We may not put two barrels next to each other
chunks.st: And one may not draw two barrels together

chunks.en: to put a pot on top of them,
chunks.explain: It looks like building.
chunks.st: in order to place a pot on them,
chunks.stMore: so that its contents will be cooked by a fire lit between the barrels.

chunks.en: We may not prop up a pot with a piece of wood,
chunks.st: And one may not prop a pot that does not stand straight with a piece of wood,
chunks.stMore: in order to prevent it from falling.

chunks.en: and the same with a door.
chunks.st: And similarly, with a door.

chunks.en: We may not lead an animal
chunks.st: And one may not lead an animal

chunks.en: with a stick on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: with a stick in the public domain on a Festival;

chunks.en: and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon allows it.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, permits it.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages argue about which bits of wood or straw we may take on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: A person may take a little stick from what is in front of him
chunks.st: On a Festival, a person may remove a sliver from a pile of straw or from similar material that is before him,

words.en: from what is in front of him

chunks.en: to clean his teeth with it.
chunks.st: in order to clean with it between his teeth.

chunks.en: And he may gather sticks from the yard and light them,
chunks.st: And he may collect straw from a courtyard and kindle it,

chunks.en: because everything in the yard is ready to be used.
chunks.st: for anything in a courtyard is considered prepared for all purposes.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: The Rabbis say:

chunks.en: He may gather only from what is in front of him, and light it.
chunks.st: He may collect these materials only from things placed before him in his house, as they are certainly prepared for all uses, and kindle them.
chunks.stMore: With regard to objects lying in his courtyard, however, as their collection takes great effort, he certainly did not have them in mind the day before, and they are therefore muktze.

words.en: from what is in front of him

mishnayos.summary: We may not make a new fire on Yom Tov. Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages also argue about how to pick out fruit before Shabbos to eat on Shabbos.

chunks.en: We may not make a new fire on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: The mishna states a different halakha: One may not produce fire,

chunks.en: not from wood,
chunks.st: neither from wood, by rubbing one piece against another;

chunks.en: not from stones,
chunks.st: nor from stones knocked against each other;

chunks.en: not from earth,
chunks.st: nor from hot dirt;
chunks.stMore: nor from tiles struck against each other;

chunks.en: and not from water.
chunks.explain: Water in a glass can focus the sun and start a fire.
chunks.st: nor from water
chunks.stMore: placed in round, glass vessels, which produces fire by focusing the rays of the sun.

chunks.he: וְאֵין מְלַבְּנִין אֶת הָרְעָפִים לִצְלוֹת בָּהֶן.
chunks.en: We may not heat tiles very hot to roast on them.
chunks.st: And similarly, one may not whiten tiles with a burning-hot heat in order to roast upon them afterward.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer also said:
chunks.st: And Rabbi Eliezer further stated the following leniency:

chunks.en: A person may stand by the place where his fruit is drying
chunks.st: A person may stand over objects in storage,
chunks.stMore: such as produce that he has for some reason previously set aside from use,

words.note: Where fruit is spread out to dry.

chunks.en: on Friday, in the Shemitah year,
chunks.st: on Shabbat eve during the Sabbatical Year,
chunks.stMore: during which no tithes are separated, which means one may take fruit on the following day without the need for any corrective measure,

chunks.en: and say: I will eat from here tomorrow.
chunks.st: and say: From here, from these fruits, I will eat tomorrow.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: Only if he marks it and says:
chunks.st: He may not eat unless he marks the pile of fruit the day before and explicitly says:

chunks.en: From here until there.
chunks.st: From here to there I will take.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Tov and Shabbos we may protect fruit, wine and oil from rain and from a leaky roof.

chunks.he: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּרוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרֻבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: On Yom Tov we may drop fruit down through a hole in the roof,
chunks.explain: This saves fruit drying on the roof from the rain.
chunks.st: One may lower produce, which had been laid out on a roof to dry, into the house through a skylight on a Festival,
chunks.stMore: in order to prevent it from becoming ruined in the rain. Although it is a strenuous activity, it is permitted do to so on a Festival in order to prevent a financial loss;

chunks.en: but not on Shabbos.
chunks.st: however, one may not do so on Shabbat.

chunks.en: We may cover fruit with things to protect it from a leak,
chunks.st: And one may cover produce inside a building with cloths to prevent damage due to a leak
chunks.stMore: in the ceiling over it,

chunks.en: and the same for jugs of wine and jugs of oil.
chunks.st: and similarly one may cover jugs of wine and jugs of oil
chunks.stMore: for the same reason.

chunks.en: And we may put a pot under a leak on Shabbos.
chunks.st: And one may place a vessel beneath a leak in order to catch the water on Shabbat, to prevent it from dirtying the house.

mishnayos.summary: Anything the Rabbis forbade on Shabbos is forbidden on Yom Tov too. The only difference between them is that on Yom Tov we may make food.

chunks.en: Anything forbidden on Shabbos as a shevus,
chunks.st: Any act for which one is liable due to a rabbinic decree made to enhance the character of Shabbat as a day of rest [shevut];

words.note: A thing the Rabbis forbade to keep Shabbos restful.

chunks.en: or as something we may choose to do,
chunks.st: or if it is notable because it is optional,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it involves an aspect of a mitzva but is not a complete mitzva;

chunks.en: or even as a mitzvah,
chunks.st: or if it is notable because it is a full-fledged mitzva,

chunks.en: if it is forbidden on Shabbos, it is forbidden on Yom Tov too.
chunks.st: if it is prohibited on Shabbat, one is liable for it on a Festival as well.

chunks.en: These are forbidden as shevus:
chunks.st: And these are the acts prohibited by the Sages as shevut:

chunks.en: We do not climb a tree,
chunks.st: One may not climb a tree on Shabbat,

chunks.en: or ride on an animal,
chunks.st: nor ride on an animal,

chunks.en: or swim in the water,
chunks.st: nor swim in the water,

chunks.en: or clap our hands,
chunks.st: nor clap his hands together,

chunks.en: or slap our legs,
chunks.st: nor clap his hand on the thigh,

chunks.en: or dance.
chunks.st: nor dance.

chunks.en: These are forbidden even though there is a bit of mitzvah in them:
chunks.st: And the following are acts that are prohibited on Shabbat and are notable because they are optional, i.e., which involve an aspect of a mitzva but are not complete mitzvot:

chunks.en: We do not judge a din Torah,
chunks.st: One may not judge,

chunks.en: or make kiddushin to get married,
chunks.st: nor betroth a woman,

chunks.en: or do chalitzah,
chunks.st: nor perform ḥalitza, which is done in lieu of levirate marriage,

words.note: Chalitzah and yibum are mitzvos for a widow whose husband had no children.

chunks.en: or do yibum.
chunks.st: nor perform levirate marriage.

chunks.en: These are forbidden even though they are a mitzvah:
chunks.st: And the following are prohibited on Shabbat despite the fact that they are notable because of the full-fledged mitzva involved in them:

chunks.en: We do not give things to the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: One may not consecrate,

words.note: Giving something to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: or promise a person's value,
chunks.st: nor take a valuation vow (see Leviticus 27),

words.note: Promising to give the value of a person to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: or make something cherem,
chunks.st: nor consecrate objects for use by the priests or the Temple,

words.note: Giving something to the Kohanim or the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: or take off terumah and maaser.
chunks.st: nor separate teruma and tithes from produce.

chunks.en: The Sages said all these about Yom Tov;
chunks.st: The Sages spoke of all these acts being prohibited even with regard to a Festival;

chunks.en: so for sure they are forbidden on Shabbos.
chunks.st: all the more so are they prohibited on Shabbat.

chunks.en: There is no difference between Yom Tov and Shabbos,
chunks.st: The general principle is: There is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat,

chunks.en: except for making food.
chunks.st: except for work involving preparation of food alone, which is permitted on a Festival but prohibited on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: On Yom Tov, our animals and things may go only as far as their owner may walk.

chunks.en: Animals and things may go only where their owner may go.
chunks.st: The status of animals and vessels on Festivals is as the feet of their owner,
chunks.stMore: meaning that one’s animals and vessels are governed by his own travel limitations on Shabbat and Festivals.

words.note: They may go only as far as that person may walk on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: If someone gives his animal to his son or to a shepherd,
chunks.st: In the case of one who delivers his animal to his son or to a shepherd before the Festival to care for it,

chunks.en: it may still go only where the owner may go.
chunks.st: these are as the feet of the owner, rather than those of the son or the shepherd.

chunks.he: כֵּלִים הַמְיֻחָדִין לְאַחַד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁבַּבַּיִת,
chunks.en: Things that belong only to one of the brothers in the house
chunks.st: Vessels that have been inherited by several brothers and have not been divided among them but are still owned jointly, if they are designated for the use of one of the brothers in the house and the other brothers have no part in them,

chunks.en: may go only where he may go.
chunks.st: these are as his feet, and they are subject to his travel limitations.

chunks.en: And things that belong to all of them
chunks.st: And as for those that are not designated for any particular brother,

chunks.en: may go only where all of them may go.
chunks.st: these are as a place where they may all go. They are limited by the travel limitations of every one of the brothers, as when one brother made a joining of Shabbat boundaries [eiruv teḥumin] and the others did not.

mishnayos.summary: When we borrow something, how far may it go on Yom Tov? It depends on when we borrowed it.

chunks.he: הַשּׁוֹאֵל כְּלִי מֵחֲבֵרוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: If someone borrows a vessel from his friend before Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One who borrows a vessel from another on the eve of a Festival,

chunks.en: it may go where the borrower may go.
chunks.st: it is as the feet of the borrower
chunks.stMore: rather than the owner, as when the Festival began the vessel established its place of rest in possession of the borrower.

chunks.en: If he borrowed it on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: However, if he borrowed it on the Festival

chunks.en: it may go only where the owner may go.
chunks.st: itself, it is as the feet of the lender,
chunks.stMore: since at the start of the Festival its place of rest was established in the possession of its owner.

chunks.en: A woman who borrowed spices from her friend
chunks.st: And similarly, a woman who borrowed spices from another
chunks.stMore: to put in a dish,

chunks.en: or water and salt for her dough:
chunks.st: or water and salt to put in her dough,

chunks.en: the food may go only where both of them may go.
chunks.st: these foods, i.e., the dish and the dough, which contain ingredients belonging to both parties, are as the feet of both of them;
chunks.stMore: they are limited by the travel limitations of both parties.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says water does not count,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda exempts one from travel limitations in the case of water,

chunks.en: because you cannot see it or hold it in the food.
chunks.st: because it has no substance in the mixture and therefore is not considered connected to the original owner.

mishnayos.summary: A glowing coal counts as a real thing, but a flame does not. Water from a well may go where its owners may go.

chunks.en: A borrowed coal may go only where its owner may go,
chunks.st: A coal that one borrowed from another on the Festival is as the feet of the owner,
chunks.stMore: and it may be carried on the Festival to any place where its owner may walk. Since it has substance, it is associated with its owner.

chunks.en: but a flame may go anywhere.
chunks.explain: A flame has nothing to hold, so it belongs to no one.
chunks.st: But a flame that one lit from another’s flame may be taken anywhere,
chunks.stMore: as it has no substance. This essential difference between a coal and a flame has additional halakhic ramifications:

chunks.en: Someone who uses a coal of hekdesh is guilty of me'ilah,
chunks.st: If one uses a coal of consecrated property for a non-consecrated purpose, he is liable for misuse
chunks.stMore: of consecrated property, since it has substance.

words.note: Wrongly using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: but a flame of hekdesh, we may not use it, but there is no me'ilah.
chunks.st: But if one uses a consecrated flame, although according to rabbinic law one may not derive benefit from it ab initio, if one did benefit from it, he is not liable for misuse,
chunks.stMore: since it does not have substance.

chunks.en: Someone who carries a coal out into the street on Shabbos is guilty,
chunks.st: Similarly, one who takes out a coal from a private domain to the public domain on Shabbat is liable
chunks.stMore: for the prohibited labor of carrying,

chunks.en: but for a flame, he is not guilty.
chunks.st: but one who takes out a flame is exempt.

chunks.en: Water from one person's well
chunks.st: With regard to a cistern of an individual,

chunks.en: may go only where that person may go.
chunks.st: water drawn from it is as the feet of the individual
chunks.stMore: who owns the cistern, and the water may be carried only to those places where its owner is permitted to walk.

chunks.en: Water from the well of the people of a town
chunks.st: And water drawn from a cistern belonging jointly to all the people dwelling in a particular town

chunks.en: may go where the people of that town may go.
chunks.st: is as the feet of the people of that town.

chunks.en: Water from a well for everyone, made for travelers from Bavel,
chunks.st: And water drawn from a cistern of those who come up to Eretz Yisrael from Babylonia, i.e., a public cistern,

chunks.en: may go wherever the person who filled it may go.
chunks.st: is as the feet of whoever fills his vessel with its water; the water has no defined boundary of its own since it is made available to all.

mishnayos.summary: If a person's fruit is in another town beyond the techum, may others bring it to him on Yom Tov?

chunks.en: If a person had fruit in another town, outside his techum,
chunks.st: With regard to one who had produce in a different city beyond the Shabbat limit,

chunks.en: and the people of that town made an eruv techumin
chunks.explain: An eruv lets a person walk farther on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: and the residents of that city
chunks.stMore: where the produce was located joined the Shabbat boundaries, enabling them to reach the owner’s home on the Festival,and they wish

chunks.en: to bring him some of his fruit,
chunks.st: to bring him some of his produce,

chunks.en: they may not bring it to him.
chunks.st: they may not bring it to him.
chunks.stMore: His produce is as his feet; since it is outside of his Shabbat limit, it may not be taken from its place.

chunks.en: But if he made an eruv too,
chunks.st: However, if the owner placed an eiruv
chunks.stMore: to enable travel to that city,

chunks.en: his fruit is like him.
chunks.st: the legal status of his produce is like his status with regard to the Shabbat limit. People from that city who also placed an eiruv may bring the produce to him, since he himself may walk to the produce and take it.

mishnayos.summary: Guests may not take home food portions unless they were given to them before Yom Tov. Which animals may we water and shecht on Yom Tov?

chunks.en: If someone invited guests from another town,
chunks.st: With regard to one who invited guests to visit him
chunks.stMore: from a town beyond his Shabbat limit, and they joined the Shabbat boundaries to enable them to reach his house,

chunks.en: they may not carry food portions home in their hands,
chunks.st: they may not carry in their hands back to their town any portions
chunks.stMore: they received from him as gifts. These portions are as the feet of the host, since they belonged to him on the eve of the Festival.

chunks.en: unless he gave them
chunks.st: This is true unless he transferred ownership of

chunks.en: their portions before Yom Tov.
chunks.st: their portions to them on the eve of the Festival,
chunks.stMore: in which case the gifts may be carried wherever the recipients may walk.

chunks.en: We may not water or shecht animals that live out in the fields,
chunks.st: On a Festival one may not water or slaughter desert animals,
chunks.stMore: which graze mainly outside the town, as they are considered muktze.

chunks.en: but we may water and shecht home animals.
chunks.st: However, one may water and slaughter domestic animals.

chunks.en: Which are home animals?
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: These are considered domestic animals:

chunks.en: Those that sleep in the town at night.
chunks.st: Those that sleep in the city at night.

chunks.en: Field animals are those that sleep out in the pasture.
chunks.st: Desert animals are those that sleep in the pasture and come into town only rarely.
